settings.heading: Who we are, why we bother, and what you can hold us to
settings.standfirst:
Oh Betty Jaletti is an American maison for the ones who take the slow way: small, useful, unreasonably pretty things, made with intention and released in considered quantities.

It is a small house, not a factory. This page says who is behind it, how a piece comes to exist, and exactly what the house promises — in plain words, with the terms written out rather than hidden behind a link.
settings.secondary_label: See what is for sale today

settings.body:
I was named for two women called Betty. One kept her paperbacks the way other people keep secrets: spines cracked, corners turned down, margins full of arguments she was winning with the author. The other believed that if a thing was worth doing, it was worth doing with the good glass, the fresh flowers, and absolutely no rush whatsoever.

Neither of them would have called any of this an aesthetic. It was simply how a day was meant to be treated: like it deserved you.

Betty Jaletti is the house I built to keep their opinion alive — for the ones who still do it the long way on purpose. Who make the coffee themselves because they have the cup for it. Who highlight in ink, without apology. Who buy the bouquet for a Tuesday.

settings.heading: We make it, or we choose it
settings.text: Some pieces the house makes by hand, in small batches. Others it chooses from makers it is proud to name. Which of the two it was is written on every piece's own page.

settings.heading: We number it
settings.text: Each piece takes its place in an edition — No. 1, No. 2 — so you know what you are holding and where it sits in the house's work.

settings.heading: We make it in considered quantities
settings.text: An edition is finished when it is right, not when it is due. That is slower, and it is the whole point: a thing made slowly is a thing worth keeping.

settings.heading: We pack it, and we answer for it
settings.text: Your parcel is packed by hand, by the house, before it goes to the post. The same house answers the email afterwards, whatever the email is about.

settings.heading: How a piece comes to exist
settings.intro: Four steps, in order, every time. None of them are quick, and that is the only interesting thing about them.
settings.footnote: Nothing here is mass-produced, and nothing here pretends to be rare that is not.

settings.heading: What “by Betty Jaletti” means — and what it does not
settings.intro:
Every piece in the house is signed … by Betty Jaletti on the first line of its description. That signature means the house presents the piece: chose it, stands behind it, and will answer for it. It does not mean the house made it.

Some pieces we make. Some we choose, and some we choose and pair. Which one it was is written on the piece's own page, every time, in its own words — so you never have to guess which kind of “handmade” you are reading.
settings.footnote: Where a piece was made by someone else, their name goes in the maker field on the product, not just in our copy. We would rather name a good French glovemaker than let you assume we are one.

settings.detail: Within the United States. Your parcel is packed by hand at the house in 3–5 business days — Express is packed first, within one business day — and then it is with the carrier. Standard arrives in 5–10 business days and costs $8.00, free on orders of $70.00 or more; Express arrives in 2–4 and costs $15.00. Checkout shows the window again before you pay, and tracking follows the parcel out of the door where it is available.

30 days from delivery, for anything unworn, unused and in its original packaging. Write to us first so the return is expected. No reason required — on a change of mind the return postage is yours, and we recommend a tracked service.

settings.term: If it arrives damaged or wrong
settings.detail: Write within 14 days of delivery with a photograph. You get a replacement or a full refund including the original shipping, and the house covers the return postage. That one is our fault, so it is our cost.
To the original payment method, within 5–10 business days of the parcel reaching us. Banks sometimes take a few days more to show it. Original shipping comes back only where the fault was ours.

We say it is a preorder before you commit, and payment is taken the day you order, not the day it ships. You may cancel any time before it ships for a full refund — one line in an email is enough. If an edition cannot be made at all, every preorder is refunded in full, unasked, and if we run past the promised window we write to you with a new date and the choice to accept it or cancel.
Your address stays with the house. We write when there is something worth telling you, and you can leave the list whenever you like without writing to ask.

settings.text: Faux suede is faux suede. We will not call it leather.
We ship within the United States only — not yet anywhere else.
No exchanges. Return it for a refund and place a new order: it is faster, and it keeps the numbering straight.
An opened bottle of fragrance cannot come back, because it cannot be resold. Unopened, within 30 days, of course it can — and if the bottle itself is faulty, write anyway.
“No. 1” is a piece's place in its edition, not a serial number on a limited run.
It is a small house. Pieces are made in considered quantities, which is why an edition is finished when it is right rather than when it is due.

settings.heading: What you can hold us to
settings.intro: Written out here rather than buried in a policy page, because a promise you have to go looking for is not much of a promise.
